entityDescription:
Lancomwas founded by a group of highly trained young IT professionals, with deep expertise and extensive experience in providing internet services. Its fields of activity are exclusively high-quality IT data center services and cloud computing.
Aiming to meet the real needs of the Greek market and the wider Balkan region on new technologies, we developed our first data center in Thessaloniki, one of the fastest growing telecommunications hubs in the region of Southeast Europe, in 100% owned facilities and on entirely owned equipment. Pursuing a growth strategy centered around offering Enterprise Class services and High Availability SLAs up to 100%, in 2014, the Company announced the creation and started operating its second Data Center, in Athens this time. As with its first data center, a location of geo-strategic importance was chosen for the Company’s second data center, which was created in Monumental Plaza building, at 44 Kifissias Ave. in Maroussi, right across from the OTE Headquarters. The entire infrastructure has been designed and implemented by meeting the latest international standards and by using all the cutting-edge technologies in cloud computing. Thus, we are able to fully meet both the current and any future market need.
Lancom’s human resources, in conjunction with the branded professional equipment we use, guarantee in the best way the superior quality of all our services. Especially regarding our manpower, we are particularly proud that we managed to create a Technical Department which inspired some of the leading engineers of Europe with the highest degree of specialization to follow.
Our main aim is maximum safety, high performance, reliability and prompt service, always providing high-quality services at low prices.

entityDescription:
PRINSUS is one of the first spinoff companies of the National Technical University of Athens (NTUA) and was developed by the Laboratory of Process Analysis and Design in the School of Chemical Engineering.The aim of PRINSUS is to transfer knowledge gained from participating in various projects funded by EU under the frame ofHorizon 2020, Horizon Europe, Interreg as well as national funds (ESPA) into useful tools, services and products available to everyone.

The core activities of PRINSUS are the provision of services to the agri-food sector in order to develop innovative products, to upgrade and evolve into new technologies and business models and to increase their competitiveness in national and international markets.
PRINSUS develops bioactive ingredients with increased antioxidant activity, bio-functionality and controlled release.
PRINSUS conducts feasibility studies, Life Cycle Assessment, Life Cycle Cost Assessment, social impact analysis and develops business plans mainly for the agrifood sector.
PRINSUS staff has been involved in numerous projects with public bodies and companies and in EU-funded international programs.
The company is interested in creating a global partnership in a wide range of scientific research projects (food, pharmaceuticalsand cosmetics industry, bio-industry, process development, eco-innovation, life cycle assessment, feasibility studies) and undertaking competitive research projects that will lead to high scientific results and commercialized products.

CRIIF Ltd is a subsidiary company of Hellenic Technology of Robotics SA, Greece (www.htr.gr). HTR is owner of an international patent related to all-metal flexible wheels for planetary rovers. HTR has supplied dozens of wheels throughout Europe and US for rover tests on mobility and energy efficiency. HTR wheels perform substantially better than US made Ti-Ni wire wheels, have fully verified cryogenic (-200C) to high temperature (+200 C) tolerance and have successfully passed endurance tests (1500 km) in fully immersed contaminated environments (Basaltic sand operation).
CRIIF Ltd has full access to HTR wheel technology and the capacity to organize the production and testing of these wheels in Cyprus.

entityDescription:
According to the Law of Greenland Parliament nr. 6 8th of June 1994 about the Greenland Institute of Natural Resources (GINR), the institute is obliged to:
- provide the scientific basis for an assessment of sustainable use of the living resources in and around Greenland as well as protecting the environment and securing the biological diversity
- advise the Greenlandic Government in the work of the Institute
- publish results of its research

On this basis the main goals of GINR are to:
- give advice based on high quality scientific research.
- foresee changes in the ecological equilibrium and the development of populations as a result of change in climate and human impact on nature.
- indicate quantitative and sustainable use of the living resources.
- advise on measures to protect the environment and ensure biological diversity.
- include local knowledge in scientific research.
- enter into open dialogue with Greenlandic communities and communicate knowledge about causal relationships in nature.
- provide suitable research facilities for the personnel and strengthen the connection between this internationally orientated workplace and theGreenlandic community.
- maintain a stable and secure working environment both physically and psychologically and establish an up-to-date physical working environment in the laboratories, field stations and boats.
- secure acquisition of necessary financial resources through the annual Finance Act as well as through external sources.
These goals are implemented by members of the staff, who:
- gather, process and assess data concerning exploitation and preservation of the living resources.
- conduct research in preparation for assessment on the living resources important for Greenland.
- contribute to studies of processes and ecological connections in nature .
- participate in surveys and innovative work in relation to the assessment ofmethods and tools used in exploiting natural resources in Greenland
- safeguard the international responsibilities that lie with Greenland within the field of research as mentioned above.
- safeguard the coordination and recording of survey and research results from related institutions which have significant influence on the living resources of Greenland and the securing of the environment and natural resources of Greenland.
The Greenland Institute of Natural Resources may undertake assignments with all or partial expenses covered by:
- other public organisations and companies
- private organisations and companies

entityDescription:
LIPOR -Municipalities Association for Sustainable Waste Management of Greater Porto - was founded in 1982 as Municipality Association and manages, recovers, and treats the municipal waste produced in eight municipalities of the Greater Porto Area: Espinho, Gondomar, Maia, Matosinhos, Porto, Póvoa de Varzim, Valongo, and Vila do Conde. At the same time, we continue to share good practices with the population, which are supported by awareness campaigns. 
Every year, we treat around 500,000 tons of municipal waste which is produced by about 1 million inhabitants. 
We are upheld by modern waste management concepts which promote the adoption of integrated systems and the minimization of waste disposal in landfill. That's why we've developed an integrated management strategy based on four key components: Multimaterial Recovery, Organic Recovery, and Energy Recovery, supported by a Landfill Site to receive the waste from processes and from previously prepared waste. 
This concept has grown naturally, and we continue to embrace new projects and services, thus strengthening its strategic path. The principles of a Circular Economy inspire us, hence, when managing the waste we receive daily, we add the three pillars of Sustainable Development: environmental, economic, and social.
Over the years, our work has been celebrated with different awards and recognitions, encouraging us to keep working towards a sustainable future.

entityDescription: Qascom (Quality and Secure Communications) is a software and systems technology provider of security applications in the satellite navigation and communications domain. Qascom operates in various sectors: Space, Transport and Government. In the space sector, Qascom offers technologies and competence in security for GNSS signals and receivers. Products range from GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite Systems) system security tools to GPS monitoring and remote tracking applications. Columbus is a suite of tools for GNSS security simulation. It can assist system designers and application developers, as well as assist in the facilitation of certification processes. Qastrack is a middleware for GNSS telematic applications, including real-time tracking and integrity monitoring. Research activities are mainly focused on GNSS signal and receiver security. Qascom has a number of publications in the field, pioneering the area of trusted location systems and location based access control. Research in GNSS receivers include the design and vulnerability assessment of tamper resistant hardware, software and cryptographic schemes. Qascom additionally performs research on anti-spoofing techniques through cryptographic integrity and authentication, both at the data and the signal level for both GNSS and augmentation systems. Services involve consulting in the area of satellite navigation systems and security analysis of critical applications. This includes vulnerability assessment, requirement analysis and risk mitigation for applications dependant on GPS. Design and integration of technologies for detection, localization and mitigation of intentional and non-intentional interference are additional services provided by Qascom for applications that rely on GNSS.

entityDescription:
Electric Vehicle Technologies
/ Hybrid Electric Aircraft Technologies
The AIT Austrian Institute of Technology actively supports the European aeronautic industry by providing technological solutions for the advancement of “More Electric Aircraft” and “Hybrid Electric Aircraft.”
As air travel continues to experience rapid growth, with one billion passengers flying within, into, or out of Europe in 2018, along with 11 million scheduled flights, we recognize the urgent need to address the environmental and sustainability challenges associated with this trend.
Our efforts encompass two key areas: the development of a electrothermal Ice Protection System for aircraft and rotorcraft, and the advancement of solid-state batteries for hybrid propulsion in regional and short to medium-range electric airliners.
In our pursuit of decarbonization, we specialize in delivering technological solutions for energy storage, electric propulsion, and electrical auxiliaries, lending our support to the European aeronautics industry. One significant area of focus is achieving energy efficiency through the implementation of innovative ice protection systems for aircraft. Within this domain, we offer comprehensive services ranging from simulating ice formation under certification-relevant environmental conditions to designing and validating performance.
Additionally, we dedicate our research efforts to the development of solid-state batteries specifically tailored for the propulsion of hybrid electric aircraft. Our services encompass modeling large-scale distributed battery systems, including the aircraft grid, as well as further advancing high-power and high-energy density battery cells, modules, and packs. These advancements are designed to handle high discharge rates while adhering to the stringent safety requirements of the aeronautics industry.
Through our commitment to technological innovation and sustainability, we aim to contribute to the transformation of the European aeronautic industry, paving the way for a greener and more efficient future in aviation.

description: Established in 2021, Astradyne is a startup at the forefront of deployable structure technology. Central to our mission is the development of lightweight, foldable photovoltaic solutions for both space and terrestrial applications, which leverage our proprietary FRET technology (Flexible Reinforced Electronics with Textile), a manufacturing process that reinforces electronic components with textile material. This breakthrough represents a significant leap in deployable systems, offering unparalleled efficiency, lightness, compactness, and versatility. Astradyne's initial focus is on the solar energy sector, where our goal is to establish a new standard in efficiency and adaptability. Our market entry is spearheaded by SolarCube, a product that embodies Astradyne's vision: a deployable solar panel that combines aesthetic sophistication with functional excellence for satellite applications. The launch of SolarCube, scheduled for 2025, directly responds to the growing and evolving needs of the space sector for more efficient and reliable energy generation solutions. On Earth, our technology finds various applications, from enhancing renewable energy sources in urban settings to powering remote and off-grid locations. Our foldable solar panels are adaptable for use in diverse environments, providing clean and sustainable energy wherever needed. Looking ahead, Astradyne is poised to expand its technological footprint. With FRET as our foundation, we are exploring new frontiers in advanced communication systems, biomedical devices, and more. Our vision is broad yet focused: to leverage our proprietary technology to meet market needs with practical and innovative solutions. Since its inception in May 2021, Astradyne has secured instrumental funding for accelerating the research and development. The team, which brings together seasoned experts from top firms and research institutions around the world, combines deep technical knowledge with a keen understanding of business strategy. This unique blend has propelled us towards significant achievements, including securing our first commercial contract and being selected as Italian Startup of the Year by a jury of investors and market experts in 2023. Currently, we are preparing to raise a seed investment by the end of 2024. This investment will be essential for the in-orbit testing and market entry of SolarCube, as well as for beginning to explore the potential of FRET technology in various products and applications.

entityDescription:
Medair is a Swiss-based international non-governmental organization (INGO) founded in 1989. Inspired by Christian faith, the mission of Medair is to alleviate human suffering in some of the world's most remote and devastated places. Medair operates with the core principle of helping people affected by natural disasters or conflict to recover with dignity. Medair adheres to the fundamental principles of the Red Cross Code of Conflict, and provides assistance based on need, regardless of race, religion, ethnicity, nationality, or political beliefs. 
Areas of Intervention:
Emergency Relief: Providing immediate assistance following disasters, such as food, shelter, and medical care.
Shelter Support: Helping families rebuild or repair their homes and communities.
Medical Care: Delivering essential healthcare services in crisis zones.
Nutrition Services: Addressing malnutrition and promoting healthy eating habits.
Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH): Ensuring access to clean water and sanitation facilities.
Cash Assistance: Empowering families to meet their basic needs quickly during crises.
Key Strengths:
Rapid Response:Medair prides itself on its ability to mobilize quickly and start delivering aid within 24 hours of a disaster.
Local Focus:They work closely with local communities and partner organizations to ensure their interventions are culturally appropriate and sustainable.
Expertise:Medair employs a team of highly skilled professionals in various fields,including health,nutrition,shelter,and water sanitation.
Commitment to Dignity:Their approach emphasizes treating people with respect and helping them rebuild their lives.

entityName: UNIVERSITY OF HEIDELBERG - Institute of Earth Sciences
entityDescription:
Goals and tasks
The overall objective of the geosciences is to understand the origin and development of the planet Earth from its formation about 4.5 billion years ago until today. The Earth's surface – and thus the human habitat – is constantly changed and reworked by complex interactions between the geosphere, the atmosphere, the hydrosphere and the biosphere. Geologic processes take place on extreme time scales – from picoseconds (as in chemical reactions on mineral surfaces) to billions of years (as in plate tectonics and biological evolution).
The geosciences have particular societal relevance not only for identification and forecasting of geohazards such as volcanic eruptions and earthquakes, but also for understanding the background of current environmental and climate change issues: the near and distant future of the earth can be predicted from the record of the geologic past. Geosciences play a central role in answering questions about the impact of humans on "system Earth", the resilience of ecosystems or the availability of natural resources. Geoscientists therefore do not only conduct basic research, but apply their research in practical manner, in particular on topics relating to sustainable environmental development and the supply of raw materials.
Research
The focus of research at the Heidelberg Institute of Earth Sciences is in the fields of solid Earth (including mineralogy, petrology, isotope geology ,and sedimentology), cosmochemistry, environmental geochemistry, paleoenvironment and paleoclimate research, paleontology, and archeometry. These research groups emphasize analyzing processes both qualitatively and quantitatively using state-of-the-art technology and instrumentation. The high analytical competence of geoscientific research in Heidelberg is demonstrated by the 2014 commissioning of the national laboratory for secondary ion mass spectrometry.

entityName: Technological University of the Shannon: Midlands Midwest
entityDescription: Technological University of the Shannon (TUS) is Ireland’s third technological university and home to 15,000 students and a staff complement of approximately 2,000, full-time and part-time, across seven campuses in Athlone, Limerick, Thurles, Clonmel, and Ennis. Established on October 1, 2021, TUS has a strong regional focus and is a key driver of development and investment across the Midlands and Midwest. The new networked university, linked by the River Shannon, borders on almost half of Ireland's 26 counties and provides unprecedented levels of access to higher education. In February 2024 TUS became a QS* 5 Star university, having achieved the highest possible number of stars to become one of the top-rated universities in the world.

entityDescription:
Solidflow BV is an SME company based in Noordwijk that is involved in product development and production of Cool Gas Generators. It is a spin-off of HDES Service & Engineering BV. Solidflow was founded in September 2023, but its history goes back to 2011 through HDES and CGG Technologies, the first CGG company in which the TNO cool gas generator technology was spun out.
Solidflow is active in high-end markets such as aerospace, defense and professional rescue systems. CO2 and oxygen generators have now been successfully developed and new gasses are currently in development. The CO2 Cool gas generator is now used in spaceflight to pressurize tanks and to inflate structures in space. The oxygen cool gas generators are developed to treat injured soldiers and to provide general practitioners with an easy and portable oxygen supply.

entityDescription: Caeli BV is a Dutch company based in Amsterdam that focuses on using satellite data in combination with advanced Ai to monitor air quality and carbon emissions globally. Their services cater to various sectors, including finance, energy, government, agriculture, health, and shipping. They provide detailed analytics on pollutants like nitrogen dioxide, ammonia, fine particles, ozone, carbon dioxide, and methane. These capabilities support environmental monitoring and assist in policy-making, highlighting Caeli BV's commitment to leveraging technology for sustainable solutions.
